evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister and tasked him with quickly arresting the economic spiral and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new finance minister faces tight time frame to tackle crises
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister and tasked him with quickly arresting the economic spiral and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong for contemporaneous appointment and policy context; the Euronews syndication preserves the Reuters text.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and at the start of Sharif's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's coalition government; the appointment was made by Sharif, though the economic crisis was inherited and IMF constraints remained external.
contrary_evidence: This appointment alone does not prove later policy quality or implementation.

evidence.claim: The budget speech said the government chose difficult decisions over political convenience, prioritized economic stability, proposed special taxes on higher incomes, created a task force against tax leakage, and imposed austerity on vehicle and foreign-travel spending.
evidence.title: Budget Speech 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The budget speech said the government chose difficult decisions over political convenience, prioritized economic stability, proposed special taxes on higher incomes, created a task force against tax leakage, and imposed austerity on vehicle and foreign-travel spending.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech from the finance ministry with explicit policy commitments.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Sharif's government and budget team; some wording is rhetorical, but it reflects the government's public policy line.
contrary_evidence: Speech rhetoric can overstate intent relative to later execution.

evidence.claim: The FY2022-23 budget was framed as a sustainable-growth budget built around widening the tax net, reducing the fiscal deficit, protecting vulnerable groups, continuing the IMF programme, targeting subsidies, and increasing taxes on wealthy people.
evidence.title: Budget in Brief 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The FY2022-23 budget was framed as a sustainable-growth budget built around widening the tax net, reducing the fiscal deficit, protecting vulnerable groups, continuing the IMF programme, targeting subsidies, and increasing taxes on wealthy people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget summary document with concrete policy priorities and fiscal strategy.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and the FY2022-23 policy cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government policy under Sharif's coalition; broader macro conditions and IMF constraints are separate from the ruler's stated priorities.
contrary_evidence: It is a plan document, so implementation has to be checked elsewhere.

evidence.claim: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.
evidence.title: Pakistan picks central bank veteran Jameel Ahmad as new governor
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a specific high-level appointment with institutional facts about the appointee.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to the Sharif government's macro-management decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The governor was appointed by the Sharif government, but the SBP remained an institutionally separate actor.
contrary_evidence: Appointment quality does not by itself prove the quality of later monetary policy.

evidence.claim: Miftah Ismail resigned as finance minister, clearing the way for Ishaq Dar to take over after months of internal pressure about key economic decisions, especially fuel prices.
evidence.title: Miftah resigns as finance minister to pave way for Dar
evidence.excerpt: Miftah Ismail resigned as finance minister, clearing the way for Ishaq Dar to take over after months of internal pressure about key economic decisions, especially fuel prices.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting on a specific cabinet turnover and the reasons attached to it.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target period and after the first half-year of Sharif's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif's coalition and party leadership choices; the precise degree of PM autonomy is partly obscured by party-family dynamics.
contrary_evidence: The resignation also reflects coalition and party politics rather than a clean managerial judgment.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet that immediately focused on stabilizing the economy and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new PM picks coalition cabinet after Khan ousted
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet that immediately focused on stabilizing the economy and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire carried by a reputable outlet; specific date and named appointments are clear.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM action, though coalition bargaining limited full control.
contrary_evidence: Coalition partners had divergent views on timing and priorities.

evidence.claim: The budget raised taxes on the rich, restricted car purchases, targeted a 4.9 percent fiscal deficit, and had already raised fuel prices by 40 percent.
evidence.title: Pakistan to raise taxes on rich, ban some car buying to secure IMF bailout
evidence.excerpt: The budget raised taxes on the rich, restricted car purchases, targeted a 4.9 percent fiscal deficit, and had already raised fuel prices by 40 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct budget reporting and specific numeric targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct policy under Sharif's government, though heavily IMF-constrained.
contrary_evidence: The same article notes the economy was already in a balance-of-payments crisis.

evidence.claim: Pakistan took important measures, and the IMF prioritized steadfast FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, social safety, and SOE/governance reforms.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Completes the Combined Seventh, and Eighth Reviews of the Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan took important measures, and the IMF prioritized steadfast FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, social safety, and SOE/governance reforms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with program details and official approval outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but mediated by the IMF program and inherited macro crisis.
contrary_evidence: The same release says FY22 policies produced overheating, deficits, and reserve erosion.

evidence.claim: The PDNA estimated large flood damages and reconstruction needs, called for a poor-first, transparent, inclusive recovery, and said the government was providing immediate relief while aiming at macroeconomic stability.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Flood Damages and Economic Losses Over USD 30 billion and Reconstruction Needs Over USD 16 billion - New Assessment
evidence.excerpt: The PDNA estimated large flood damages and reconstruction needs, called for a poor-first, transparent, inclusive recovery, and said the government was providing immediate relief while aiming at macroeconomic stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank assessment with explicit recovery principles and quantified damage estimates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable through government relief design and response, but heavily constrained by disaster magnitude and donor reliance.
contrary_evidence: The assessment says losses and poverty impacts were still increasing and external support would be essential.

evidence.claim: Five World Bank projects supported flood recovery, housing reconstruction, crop restoration, social protection delivery, and health services for mothers and children, including cash transfers and strengthened disaster-response capacity.
evidence.title: Pakistan: World Bank Approves $1.692 Billion for 5 Projects to Support the People of Sindh in the Flood-Affected Areas
evidence.excerpt: Five World Bank projects supported flood recovery, housing reconstruction, crop restoration, social protection delivery, and health services for mothers and children, including cash transfers and strengthened disaster-response capacity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank announcement with concrete project terms and funding amounts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: the Sharif government was the implementing counterpart, though execution depended on the Bank and provinces.
contrary_evidence: This is implementation architecture more than proof of completed outcomes by year-end.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.
